headline.title: Sam Altman responds to ‘incendiary’ New Yorker article after attack on his home
headline.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed concerns raised in a New Yorker profile questioning his trustworthiness, following an incident where his home was reportedly attacked. In a blog post, he responded to both the article and the attack, aiming to clarify his position.

articles.title: Your article about AI doesn’t need AI art
articles.summary: The New Yorker's profile of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman features an unsettling AI-generated illustration that depicts a cluster of distorted faces around him. The artwork has drawn criticism for its eerie representation and lack of coherence with Altman's likeness.

articles.title: My baby deer plushie told me that Mitski’s dad was a CIA operative
articles.summary: The article discusses a friend's surprising text about singer Mitski's father allegedly being a CIA operative, which sparked curiosity and intrigue. It reflects on the unexpected nature of such claims and the reactions they provoke.

articles.title: How Iran out-shitposted the White House
articles.summary: In the early stages of the conflict with Iran, the Iranian regime's state media effectively utilized social media to disseminate impactful footage of the war, contrasting with the White House's less serious online presence. This strategic communication approach allowed Iran to dominate the narrative in the digital space during the conflict.

articles.title: Your Push Notifications Aren’t Safe From the FBI
articles.summary: The FBI has the capability to access and monitor push notifications, raising concerns about user privacy and data security. Additionally, Iran's internet blackout has now surpassed 1,000 hours, and cryptocurrency scams have led to a record amount of financial losses for Americans.

articles.title: How the Internet Broke Everyone’s Bullshit Detectors
articles.summary: The article discusses the challenges faced by verification systems in distinguishing real content from misinformation due to the rise of AI-generated images and restricted satellite data. It highlights how these developments have compromised people's ability to discern truth online.
